verdict.rationale: Keycloak's own docs cover hosted sign-in (SSO login across applications), sign-up ('Allowing users to self-register', with terms and conditions during registration), and profile management through a prebuilt Account Console where users update their profile, change passwords and set up 2FA. Themes are documented as the way to customize look and feel. One community user notes you can't easily add a custom page next to the login flow without extending Keycloak, which limits customization depth but does not contradict the capability. missing for 10: in-depth evidence of how far theme customization of the login, registration and account pages goes, no embeddable UI components (only hosted pages), and no independent hands-on corroboration of the hosted pages in production.

support.subject: As a developer, I can ship production sign-in, sign-up, and profile management with prebuilt, customizable UI components or hosted pages

citations.quote: Once logged-in to Keycloak, users don't have to login again to access a different application.
Allowing users to self-register ... Requiring user to agree to terms and conditions during registration
Through the account management console users can manage their own accounts. They can update the profile, change passwords, and setup two-factor authentication.
As a user in the Account Console, you can manage your account including modifying your profile, adding two-factor authentication, and including identity provider accounts.
Creating themes and providers to customize the Keycloak server
